name: GateForm
author: gateform

sections.description:
The plugin loads client.js from the GateForm service into
WordPress forms and validates a one-time token on the server. The secret key is
stored only in the WordPress database and is never printed into HTML.

Website: gateform.ru
Documentation: gateform.ru/docs
Support: info@gateform.ru

Protected forms:

  • comment form;
  • login to the dashboard and the site through wp-login.php;
  • registration form;
  • Contact Form 7 (CAPTCHA and the [gateform] tag);
  • WPForms;
  • Gravity Forms;
  • Ninja Forms;
  • Elementor Pro Forms;
  • Formidable Forms;
  • Fluent Forms;
  • WooCommerce: checkout, login, and registration;
  • custom forms by CSS selectors.

Contact widget (does not require a secret key):

  • when a widget ID (w_...) is set in the settings, the widget code is added
    to the site footer (wp_footer) automatically;
  • the [gateform_widget] shortcode is also supported.

The “Protected by GateForm” label with a link to the website and the logo is
displayed in Contact Form 7 forms and can be disabled with the
gateform_cf7_branding filter.

Form field values are not sent to the validation service. Visitor IP addresses
are not stored by the plugin.

External services

This plugin connects to the external GateForm service at https://gateform.ru
to provide CAPTCHA protection for WordPress forms and an optional contact widget.

GateForm is used for:

  • Loading the CAPTCHA client script (client.js) on pages with protected forms.
  • Loading the contact widget script (widget.js) when a widget ID is configured.
  • Validating a one-time CAPTCHA token when a protected form is submitted.

The service is required for the CAPTCHA and contact-widget features.

CAPTCHA validation

When a visitor opens a page with a protected form, the browser loads
https://gateform.ru/client.js. The script may collect behavioral signals needed
to distinguish human visitors from automated requests.

When a visitor submits a protected form, the plugin sends the public site key,
the secret key, and the one-time CAPTCHA token to
https://gateform.ru/api/v1/validate over HTTPS.

The plugin does not send form field values, comments, message content, or visitor
IP addresses to GateForm.

Contact widget

When a widget ID is configured, the browser loads https://gateform.ru/widget.js.
The widget may display a contact form, chat, links to social networks, or other
contact options, depending on the website owner’s GateForm widget settings.

If the website owner enables a contact form or chat, information entered by the
visitor in that widget — for example, name, email address, phone number, or
message — may be sent to GateForm to process and deliver the contact request.
No visitor data is sent by this plugin itself; data handling depends on the
widget configuration selected by the website owner.

Service terms and privacy

  • Terms of Service: https://gateform.ru/agreement
  • Privacy Policy for website visitors: https://gateform.ru/privacy/visitors
  • GateForm website: https://gateform.ru
sections.installation:
1. Upload the gateform folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the ZIP file
    through “Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin”.
  2. Activate the plugin on the “Plugins” screen.
  3. Open “Settings → GateForm”.
  4. Enter the public key (site_key) and the secret key (secret_key).
  5. Select the forms you want to protect.
  6. Optionally enter the widget ID (w_...) — the widget code appears in the
    site footer immediately.

Keys are created in the GateForm dashboard. The site domain must be specified in
the key settings.
sections.faq:
How do I add the CAPTCHA to Contact Form 7?

Enable “Contact Form 7” in the plugin settings. You can add the [gateform] tag
to the form — it prints the hidden token field and the GateForm label. If the tag
is not added, client.js connects to the form automatically and adds the field
itself.

Why is the CAPTCHA not visible in the Contact Form 7 form?

GateForm uses an invisible behavioral check and shows the “I am not a robot”
button only when a bot is suspected. The hidden gf_token field and the GateForm
label are added automatically.

Does the plugin need external services or a CDN?

No. Only the script from your GateForm instance is loaded.

What happens if the validation service is unavailable?

Forms are rejected by default (secure mode). Enable “Accept forms without
validation (fail-open)” if not losing submissions is more important.

Is the plugin compatible with page caching?

Yes. The script is added to the page footer, and the token is requested at the
moment the form is submitted.

Where is the secret key stored?

In the wp_options table. It is not printed into HTML and is not passed to
JavaScript.

Can I use only the contact widget?

Yes. Enter only the widget ID w_... in the settings — the widget script is
printed in the site footer immediately. No secret key is required for it.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Unified plugin: CAPTCHA plus the contact widget.
  • Full Contact Form 7 integration: the [gateform] tag, validation through
    wpcf7_validate, the hidden token field, and branding with a link to
    gateform.ru.
  • The [gateform_widget] shortcode for placing the contact widget anywhere on
    the site.
  • Logo and website link in the admin screen and in Contact Form 7 forms.
  • Validation result caching within a single request.

1.1.0

  • Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Ninja Forms, Elementor Pro,
    Formidable Forms, Fluent Forms, and WooCommerce support.
  • Login protection through wp-login.php.
  • Custom form CSS selectors and the gateform_validate_token filter.
  • Fail-open mode and per-integration settings.

1.0.0

  • First release: comments, login, registration, and fail-open mode.
